rationale: Lycopolitan ⲍ-onset variant of ϩⲣⲱⲙⲁⲓⲟⲥ (Greek Ῥωμαῖος). Second of the four great Manichaean kingdoms = the Roman Empire.

Tentatively identified as the Lyc./corrupted Coptic rendering of Ἀξωμῖται 'Aksumites' — the third of the canonical four Manichaean kingdoms. The form is unusual; possibly reflects a scribal corruption. Confidence moderate; awaits parallels.
The fourth great kingdom in the Manichaean four-kingdoms scheme, identified in Eastern Manichaean sources with the land of silk (China). Preserved as proper noun.
Lycopolitan plural form of ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'king/kingship' (cf. attested ⲡⲟⲣⲟ). The -ⲁⲓ̈ ending forms a regular Lyc. plural. Distinct from ⲙⲛⲧⲣ̄ⲡⲣⲁⲓ̈ 'kingships' (abstract plural) which appears in line 25.
Standard Manichaean Christological epithet combining contracted Lyc. ⲥⲏⲣ (= σωτήρ 'Savior') with Greek ἀγαθός 'good.' Used to introduce dominical citations, here a Matt 10:42 parallel.

Verbal form of uncertain etymology in line 16. Context (object: ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲧⲙⲏⲉ 'inward to the truth') requires a verb of leading/guiding/bringing. Possibly Lyc. reflex of a causative-bring stem. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.

proposed_english: they busy themselves with / they are absorbed in
rationale: 3pl. verbal form in line 26 governing ⲛ̄ⲧⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ ⲙⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'with the desire of the world.' Pairs syntactically with ⲥⲉⲃⲓⲣⲁⲩϣ ⲍⲁ ⲡⲃⲓⲟⲥ 'they are anxious for life' as a worldly-preoccupation doublet. Etymology unclear; possibly from ⲣ̄-ⲃⲗⲗⲉ 'be preoccupied' or ⲃⲱⲗ in transferred sense. Confidence low.

Verbal form in 'that one shall ⲉⲛⲉⲉϩ before God' (line 9). Likely future of ⲱⲛⲉϩ 'live' (giving 'shall live before God' — eschatological reward) or qualitative of ⲱϩⲉ 'stand' (giving 'shall stand before God'). Both fit context. Confidence moderate.
Lyc. variant of ⲣⲟⲟⲩϣ 'care, anxiety' (verbalized form). Line 27 ⲥⲉⲃⲓⲣⲁⲩϣ ⲍⲁ ⲡⲃⲓⲟⲥ 'they are anxious for (this) life' — Synoptic-style polemic against worldly μέριμνα (Matt 6:25-34).

Standard Manichaean technical phrase paired with ⲡⲣⲉⲛ ⲙ̄ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲧⲉ 'the name of God' as the dual ground for hospitality-acts that earn the supreme reward. Recurs three times on this page (lines 8, 15, 18).
